not_evidence: HAND-WRITTEN. Every harvested example is a real config, but none of them combines a clean provider/model with an output_schema and a documented invoke call, so this one exists to show the whole authoring path in one place. It is NOT proof the platform accepts it — a live create + invoke is (see how_to_verify_on_staging).
teaches: the create shape: create_agent builds the { config: {...} } wrapper for you, so pass the definition itself
output_schema is a { field: description } MAP, not JSON Schema — and the invoke result is still a STRING regardless, MARKDOWN-FENCED, so a bare JSON.parse throws (see expected_invoke_shape)
api_key names an account secret (CLAUDE_API_KEY), it is not the key itself; api_key_source "system" lets the platform resolve it
shared "" is the live default (148/189 configs) — "private" and "team" are also in use, and no live config uses "public"
the subject is SERVER-generated as ms.hub.config.agent.<md5-of-config>, so creating the same config twice returns 409 agent exists:<subject>
the {id} path param for get/update/delete is the uuid SUFFIX of the subject — not the subject, and not config.id

config.name: Submission Triage (MCP verification)
config.description: Classifies an inbound insurance submission and states whether it is in appetite.
config.behaviour:
You triage inbound commercial insurance submissions for an Australian broker.

Given a submission, decide:
1. the class of business,
2. whether it is in appetite (decline anything with an aggregate sum insured above 50,000,000 AUD or a risk address outside Australia),
3. one sentence of reasoning.

Answer with the fields described by the output schema and nothing else.

output_schema.class_of_business: The class of business, e.g. 'Builders Risk' or 'Professional Indemnity'.

invoke.subject: <the subject returned by create_agent>
invoke.prompt: Submission: Ridgeline Constructions Pty Ltd, builders risk, project value 2,500,000 AUD, risk address 42 Example St, Melbourne VIC 3000.

expected_invoke_shape.verified: 2026-07-29 on staging, invoked twice with this exact config.
expected_invoke_shape.note: The result is a STRING even with output_schema set — and it is NOT raw JSON. It comes back MARKDOWN-FENCED, so a bare JSON.parse THROWS. Extract the object first: JSON.parse(String(result).match(/\{[\s\S]*\}/)[0]). In a flow that goes in an eval node between the agent node and any condition.
expected_invoke_shape.actual_result_observed:
```json
{
  "class_of_business": "Builders Risk",
  "in_appetite": true,
  "reason": "Sum insured of 2,500,000 AUD is below the 50,000,000 AUD threshold and risk address is located in Melbourne, Australia."
}
```
expected_invoke_shape.what_the_docs_used_to_say: Both this MCP and quiva-flows-mcp said the result was a JSON-encoded string to be JSON.parse'd. That advice fails as written — the fence has to come off first. Corrected in both.

max_tokens_trap.symptom: create_agent succeeds, the config stores and reads back perfectly, and then invoke_agent returns 400 EXECUTION_ERROR: thinking_tokens must be less than max_tokens (thinking=8000, max=1024).
max_tokens_trap.cause: bellerophon-workforce/cmd/agent-service/service/process_invoke.go:893-902 — when ENABLE_NATIVE_THINKING is on and the model supports thinking, the service INJECTS thinking_enabled=true and thinking_tokens=8000, but only for fields the caller left unset. It never compares that injected budget against the caller's max_tokens, so any llm_config.max_tokens at or below 8000 fails at invoke time.
max_tokens_trap.why_it_is_a_trap: Nothing rejects it at create time — the config is valid, stored and served. 1024 and 2048 are the natural values to pick. Hit live 2026-07-29 with max_tokens: 1024, which is why this example now uses 16000.
max_tokens_trap.live_blast_radius: 8 of the 144 live configs with an llm_config set max_tokens <= 8000 with no thinking_tokens, so they cannot currently be invoked at all (Anthropic Model Selector 1000, Decision-Making Assistant x3 at 1024, email-priority-organizer 2000, JavaScript Code Review Agent 2000, weather-historian 2000).
three_ways_out: set max_tokens comfortably above 8000 (what this example does)
set llm_config.thinking_tokens explicitly to something below max_tokens — injection only fills fields left nil
omit max_tokens entirely and let the provider default apply

provider_rules_that_bite: invoke_agent accepts only llm_provider "claude" or "anthropic" — anything else returns 400 "unsupported provider" (hub-service/handler/agents.go)
STORING another provider is fine: 12 gemini, 6 openai and 1 workforce config are live on staging right now. Creating and invoking have different rules
use platform model aliases (claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6) rather than dated ids where possible
how_to_verify_on_staging: create_agent — keep the returned `subject`; the {id} for later calls is subject.split('.').pop()
invoke_agent with that subject and the prompt above (THIS SPENDS LLM TOKENS — one claude-haiku-4-5 call). Keep llm_config.max_tokens above 8000 or this step 400s — see max_tokens_trap
get_agent with the path id to confirm the stored config round-tripped

open the agent editor at https://app.microstrate.io/en/hub/agents/edit/<subject with every "." replaced by "+"> — NOT /en/hub/agents, which has no +page.svelte. Agents are labelled "Assistants" in the UI
create_agent a second time with the identical config to confirm the documented 409 (the subject is an md5 of the config)
delete_agent to clean up — then note that get_agent on the deleted subject returns a HOLLOW all-empty config rather than 404
